title: How to search your chat history in ChatGPT on Mac: the 2026 desktop app steps
metaTitle: How to Search Your Chat History in ChatGPT on Mac
description: How to search your chat history in ChatGPT on Mac: use Search chats in the sidebar, ⌘F inside a chat, and fixes for missing chats.
targetKeyword: how to search your chat history in chatgpt on mac
intro: To search your chat history in ChatGPT on Mac, open the sidebar, click Search chats, and type a phrase you remember from the conversation. To search inside one open chat instead, press ⌘F, which searches only that chat.
tldr: Click Search chats in the left sidebar to search your chat history.
Press ⌘F to search only the chat that is open, then ⌘G and ⌘⇧G to move between matches.
Search chats has no default shortcut. Assign one in Settings > Keyboard Shortcuts.
Use Search projects from the Projects view, and pin the chats you open daily with ⌘⌥P.
If chats seem missing after an update, check Recents and Projects. Community reports from July 2026 describe a fault with no confirmed fix.

blocks.text: Start by checking which ChatGPT app you have open. OpenAI's new desktop app for Mac combines Chat, Work and Codex in one place. The older app is called ChatGPT Classic. The names in this guide match the new app, so check the app name before you look for a button that is not there.
Search chats from the sidebar

Your main search sits in the left sidebar. Look for the option named Search chats. OpenAI's command reference lists it as a sidebar option with no default shortcut. So you click it first, and you can add a shortcut later if you use it every day.

A hidden sidebar hides Search chats too. Press ⌘B to show or hide the sidebar. OpenAI's reference also lists ⌘⇧S for the same job. If neither key changes anything, confirm that you are in the new desktop app.
What search looks for in your history

OpenAI's Projects help page says to open Search chats when you remember a phrase or a branch name but not the title. That suggests search reads the words inside your messages, not just the titles. OpenAI's main Help Center did not load during our research, so confirm the matching rules yourself.

blocks.title: Test it once
blocks.text: Pick a chat you know well. Search for a distinctive word from the middle of one of its replies. If the chat appears, search reads message text. If it does not, rely on titles and the phrases you remember.
Common words return too much. A word like help or code can match many chats. Use a name, a place, a product or an error message instead. Those terms narrow the list fast.
Find a word inside the chat you have open
Press ⌘F to search only the chat on your screen. OpenAI's reference says Find in chat searches only the open chat, not other chats. Use it when you know the right thread and want one answer from it.
Press ⌘G to jump to the next match. Press ⌘⇧G to go back to the previous one. Those two keys let you scan a long thread without scrolling past every line.

Say you planned a trip in one long thread and remember asking about passport rules. Open that thread, press ⌘F, and type passport. Then press ⌘G until you reach the answer. You never leave the chat, and you never need its title.
Search Projects and archived chats

Projects group related chats together. From the Projects view, use Search projects to find a project by name. Open the project, then look for your chat inside it. To learn how projects work, read [how to create a project in ChatGPT on Mac](/how-to/create-a-project-in-chatgpt).

Archived chats leave the main list, so a normal search can seem to skip them. Archive a chat with ⌘⇧A when you want it out of the way. To bring one back, open Settings with ⌘, and look for archived chats. OpenAI's Projects page gives two paths. One says Settings > Archived chats. The other says Settings > Data Controls > Archived chats. Check which one your app shows.

Pin the threads you open every day with ⌘⌥P. Pinned chats give you a quick way back, so you search less. The full sidebar steps are in [how to pin a chat in ChatGPT on Mac](/how-to/pin-a-chat-in-chatgpt).
Set a shortcut for Search chats

Search chats has no default shortcut, so you add one yourself. Press ⌘, to open Settings. Then open Keyboard Shortcuts, which the reference lists under ⌘/. Find Search chats in the list and assign the key combination you want.

Pick a combination that no other app uses. Keys that combine ⌘ and ⌥ are less likely to clash with common shortcuts than a single letter with ⌘ alone. Test the new shortcut in a chat before you depend on it.

blocks.text: Common mistakes that hide your chats

items: Searching for a title you do not remember. Search a phrase from the message instead.
Expecting ⌘F to cover every chat. It covers only the open chat.
Looking for archived chats in the main list. They live under Settings.
Trusting one shortcut list. The command reference lists ⌘K as Open command menu, but the Projects page says Cmd or Ctrl plus K searches past chats. Check ⌘/ in your own app.
Mixing up the two apps. ChatGPT Classic is the older app, and it can look different from the new one.

blocks.text: Why chats can look missing after an update

Some users reported a problem in July 2026. After they updated the Mac app, the mode menu showed only Work and Codex. Their existing chats and Projects did not appear. The community thread covers builds 26.707.31428, 26.707.51957 and 26.707.72221.
The thread reports no confirmed fix, and no OpenAI staff member had replied when it was read. Affected users switched to the web version to reach their chats. That is a workaround, not a repair.

An OpenAI_Support reply posted August 20, 2026 suggests other checks. Update the desktop app. Select ChatGPT from the top-left switcher. Look for previous chats in Recents, and check Projects. The reply names no build and does not mention search, so it may not match your version.

blocks.title: Community reports, not official fixes
blocks.text: Treat these reports as clues, not a guaranteed fix. Compare your build number with the thread before you act on any step it describes.
Locked chats and third-party search tools

OpenAI's release notes list locked chats, announced October 20, 2026. A locked chat opens with a 4-digit account PIN or supported device authentication. The notes do not say whether locked chats appear in search, so test that on one of your own.

A third-party extension called AI Toolbox adds its own Search History on chatgpt.com. It is not a ChatGPT feature. Its tutorial gives Cmd+Shift+F on Mac for that extension. Use ChatGPT's own sidebar search first, and treat the extension as a separate tool.
A quick routine when a chat is hard to find

Start with a phrase, not a title. If nothing appears, open the chat you think holds it and press ⌘F. Next, check Projects. Then check archived chats. Last, look in Recents, as the support reply suggests. Each check rules out one place, so you stop guessing.
Keep the chats you reach most often pinned. Then your searches cover only the threads you do not open daily. That keeps the results list short and the matches easier to read.
What to do next

If you want to remove old threads, read [how to delete a chat in ChatGPT on Mac](/how-to/delete-a-chat-in-chatgpt). It explains one chat, all chats, and what stays behind. If you want a copy of your history first, read [how to export your ChatGPT data on Mac](/how-to/export-your-chatgpt-data-in-chatgpt).

If you want new conversations kept out of your history, see [how to turn off chat history in ChatGPT on Mac](/how-to/turn-off-chat-history-in-chatgpt). Check that page for what the setting does and does not cover.

faq.question: Is there a keyboard shortcut to search chat history in ChatGPT on Mac?
faq.answer: Not by default. OpenAI's command reference says Search chats has no default shortcut. You can assign one under Settings > Keyboard Shortcuts. Find in chat is ⌘F, but it searches only the chat you have open.

faq.question: Can ⌘F search all my ChatGPT chats?
faq.answer: No. OpenAI's command reference says Find in chat searches only the open chat, not other chats. To search across your history, use the sidebar option named Search chats.

faq.question: Does search find words inside messages or only titles?
faq.answer: OpenAI's Projects page says to use search when you remember a phrase or a branch name but not the title. That suggests message text counts. The main Help Center did not load during our research, so test it on a chat you know.

faq.question: Why is Search chats missing from my sidebar?
faq.answer: Press ⌘B first to show the sidebar. Then confirm you are in the new desktop app, not ChatGPT Classic. A July 2026 community thread reports missing chats and Chat mode on several builds, and no confirmed fix appeared there.

faq.question: Where do archived chats go?
faq.answer: OpenAI's Projects page gives two paths for restoring them. One says Settings > Archived chats. The other says Settings > Data Controls > Archived chats. Open Settings and use whichever path your app shows.

faq.question: Does ⌘K open search in ChatGPT on Mac?
faq.answer: The sources disagree. The command reference lists ⌘K as Open command menu, while the Projects page says Cmd or Ctrl plus K searches past chats. Press ⌘/ in your app to see what your build does.

faq.question: Can I search locked chats?
faq.answer: OpenAI's release notes announced locked chats on October 20, 2026. A locked chat opens with a 4-digit account PIN or supported device authentication. The notes do not say whether search covers locked chats.

task: Find an old ChatGPT chat on Mac
appliesTo: ChatGPT desktop app for Mac, 2026 builds with Chat, Work and Codex
requirements: A Mac with the new ChatGPT desktop app installed
A ChatGPT account signed in on that Mac
The chat or project you want to find under the same account
Optional: a key combination you want to assign to Search chats

steps.name: Confirm you are in the new desktop app
steps.text: Open ChatGPT from the Dock or your Applications folder. The new desktop app combines Chat, Work and Codex. The older app is called ChatGPT Classic. If your window looks different from these steps, check which app you have open before you keep searching.
steps.tip: Keep only the app you use. Two copies make it easy to open the wrong one.

steps.name: Show the sidebar
steps.text: Look at the left edge of the window. If the sidebar is hidden, press ⌘B. OpenAI's reference also lists ⌘⇧S for the same action. Both keys toggle the sidebar on and off.
steps.tip: A hidden sidebar also hides Search chats, so check this first.

steps.name: Click Search chats
steps.text: In the sidebar, click Search chats. OpenAI's command reference describes it as a sidebar option with no default shortcut. Read the label, because the icon and spacing may vary by build.
steps.tip: A third-party tutorial describes the native search as a magnifying glass in the left sidebar. Trust the label first.

steps.name: Type a phrase you remember
steps.text: Type a word or phrase from the chat, not a guess at its title. OpenAI's Projects page says search works when you remember a phrase or a branch name. Add a few distinctive words to narrow the results.
steps.tip: A name, a place or an error message makes a better search term than a common word.

steps.name: Open the matching chat
steps.text: Scroll the results and click the one that fits. The chat opens in the main window. Read the first lines to confirm it is the right thread before you copy anything out of it.
steps.tip: If the first match is wrong, try the next result before you change your search.

steps.name: Search inside one chat with Find in chat
steps.text: Open the chat you think holds the answer. Press ⌘F to open Find in chat. The search covers only that chat, not your other chats. Type a word and read the highlighted matches in the thread.
steps.tip: Use this after you have found the right chat. It does not replace Search chats.

steps.name: Move between matches
steps.text: Press ⌘G to jump to the next match. Press ⌘⇧G to jump back to the previous match. Keep the chat open while you move, so the highlights stay on screen.
steps.tip: Shift adds the reverse direction, so ⌘⇧G goes back.

steps.name: Search your Projects
steps.text: Open the Projects view from the sidebar. Use Search projects to find a project by its name. Open the project and look for your chat inside it. Projects keep related chats together, so this search narrows a large list fast.
steps.tip: If a project seems missing, read the update section above before you assume the chat is gone.

steps.name: Find archived chats
steps.text: Archive a chat with ⌘⇧A to take it out of the main list. To find archived chats, open Settings with ⌘, and look for archived chats. OpenAI's pages give two paths, Settings > Archived chats and Settings > Data Controls > Archived chats. Use the one your app shows.
steps.tip: Archiving is not deleting. Use the Settings path to bring a chat back.

steps.name: Assign a shortcut to Search chats
steps.text: Press ⌘, to open Settings. Open Keyboard Shortcuts, which the command reference lists under ⌘/. Find Search chats in the list, set a key combination, and test it in a chat.
steps.tip: Choose a combination you do not use in any other app.

steps.name: Pin the chats you reach most
steps.text: Open a chat you use often and press ⌘⌥P to pin it. Pinned chats stay easy to reach, so you search for them less. To rename a chat with a clearer title, press ⌘⌥R.
steps.tip: Rename a chat to a phrase you will remember, such as a project or client name.

troubleshooting.problem: Search chats is not in the sidebar
troubleshooting.fix: Press ⌘B to show the sidebar, then confirm you are in the new desktop app. If it is still missing, your build may match the July 2026 reports. Note your build number, compare it with the community thread, and use the web version as a stopgap.

troubleshooting.problem: Older chats do not show in the list
troubleshooting.fix: Check Recents and Projects, as the August 2026 support reply suggests. Then check archived chats under Settings. That reply names no build number, so confirm each check in your own app.
It searches only the open chat. Open the chat you think holds the words, then press ⌘F again. For other chats, use Search chats in the sidebar.

troubleshooting.problem: Search returns nothing for a chat title
troubleshooting.fix: Search a phrase from the body of the chat instead. OpenAI's Projects page says phrase search helps when you do not remember the title.
The sources disagree on ⌘K. Press ⌘/ to open the shortcut list, use the key listed for Search chats, or assign your own.
Archiving is not deleting. Open Settings with ⌘, and look for archived chats. Use whichever path your app shows, since the two OpenAI pages name different paths.
